# shadow/no-signal-write-in-render-body

Disallow writing external signals or stores while a component renders.

`recommended`

## Why

A component body runs once to build its DOM. Writing a signal that lives outside the component from that body re-notifies readers while they are still being created, produces different output on the server and the client, and can loop. Initialize state with the value you want, write from an event handler, or move the write into `onMount` / `useEffect`.

## Incorrect

```tsx
const [visited, setVisited] = useSignal(false);
function Page() {
  setVisited(true);
  return <p>Hi</p>;
}
```

## Correct

```tsx
const [visited, setVisited] = useSignal(false);
function Page() {
  onMount(() => setVisited(true));
  return <p>Hi</p>;
}
```

```tsx
function Counter() {
  const [count, setCount] = useSignal(0);
  return <button onClick={() => setCount(count() + 1)}>{count}</button>;
}
```

## Disabling

Disable one line with `// eslint-disable-next-line shadow/no-signal-write-in-render-body`, a block with `/* eslint-disable shadow/no-signal-write-in-render-body */` and `/* eslint-enable shadow/no-signal-write-in-render-body */`, or a whole file with the block form at its top. When the write is a deliberate one-time registration that must happen while the component is created, such as announcing to a shared store that it mounted before its children read it.

## Notes

- Signals created in the same component are not reported: seeding your own state is harmless.
- Callbacks that run immediately (IIFEs, `batch`, `untrack`, `array.map`) count as part of the render body; event handlers and effects do not.

## Messages

- `writeInRender`: `{{name}}` writes state while `{{component}}` renders. Write from an event handler, `onMount` or `useEffect` instead.

## Configs

| Config | Setting |
| --- | --- |
| `recommended` | warn |
| `strict` | error |
| `migration` | warn |
| `dusk` | warn |
